Leave-one-out cross-validation that leaves out whole individuals or groups

Source: R/loo-hazard.R
loo_hazard.Rd

Estimates how well a model fitted with fit_hazard() predicts data it was not fitted to, by Pareto-smoothed importance sampling (PSIS-LOO), leaving out one unit at a time: an individual, or a group of individuals.

Usage

loo_hazard(fit, unit = NULL)

Arguments

fit

A brmsfit, a model fitted with fit_hazard().

unit

An optional character string, the unit to leave out: "id" for the individual, or one of the groupings of the model's group-level terms, such as "trial", or "trial:tank" for the tanks of (1 | trial/tank). NULL (the default) chooses as described above.

Value

A loo object (see loo::loo()) with one pointwise value per unit, and an extra element unit naming the unit.

Details

The model is fitted one row per individual and interval at risk, so brms::loo() would leave out one interval, and ask how well the model predicts the rest of an individual's exposure from its beginning, which is nearly always easy. Here the pointwise log-likelihood is summed within each unit, which given the parameters is that unit's log-likelihood exactly, and the unit is left out whole.

Where individuals share a group-level effect in the model, such as a random intercept per trial, leaving out one individual still leaves its trial's effect, estimated from the other individuals of the trial, in the fit, and the prediction looks better than it would for a new trial. So by default the unit is the coarsest grouping variable whose levels individuals share, with a message saying so, and otherwise the individual. Nested groupings, such as tanks within trials, are handled by this: leaving out a trial takes its tanks with it. Asking for a finer unit gives a warning that the coarser grouping's effect stays in the fit, which is appropriate when the data to be predicted come from the same levels of it, and optimistic when they come from new ones.

Crossed groupings, such as families spread across trials, have no default: no single unit removes the effects of both, and leaving out trials answers how well the model predicts new trials of known families, while leaving out families answers how well it predicts new families. The unit must then be given.

Leaving out a large unit can change the posterior too much for PSIS to stand in for refitting. Where the Pareto k diagnostic of any unit is above the threshold for the number of draws, a warning says so, and kfold_hazard() gives an exact estimate by refitting.

Models compared with loo::loo_compare() must be cross-validated with the same unit.

References

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A. and Gabry, J. (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing 27, 1413-1432.

Vehtari, A., Simpson, D., Gelman, A., Yao, Y. and Gabry, J. (2024). Pareto smoothed importance sampling. Journal of Machine Learning Research 25(72), 1-58.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# a model fitted to a small ramping trial: 20 individuals warmed from 20 to 35
# degrees over 60 minutes and checked every 10, in two trials (see fit_hazard())
path   <- data.frame(path_id = "A", time = c(0, 60), temp = c(20, 35))
checks <- data.frame(path_id = "A", time = seq(0, 60, by = 10))
ind    <- data.frame(id = 1:20, path_id = "A", event = 1, mass = runif(20, 8, 12),
                     trial = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 10),
                     t_upper = sample(seq(10, 60, 10), 20, replace = TRUE))
long   <- build_hazard_data(ind, path, "interval", covariates = c("mass", "trial"),
                            checks = checks)

fit <- fit_hazard(long, "exp", dpar_formulas = list(loga = ~ 1 + (1 | trial)))
loo_hazard(fit)                 # leaves out one trial at a time
} # }
